feedback: D1 is a strong catalogue. You quoted the exact evidence line for the SQL injection in login.php (the WHERE clause with string concatenation), the unsalted MD5 hashing, the alg:none acceptance branch (lines 41-43), the hardcoded secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019, the missing token expiry, the XXE in 04-import-xxe.xml, the open redirect with the 02:21:13 capture, and the cookie missing Secure and SameSite. Your OWASP categories slip in a few places (alg:none is A07 CWE-347 not A01 CWE-287, no-expiry is A07, the cookie is A05) but the CWE and the evidence line are right so I credited those findings. Two real findings are missing: the STORED XSS that beacons the cookie to 185.220.101.9:8443 at 02:18:47 (you logged a reflected XSS on the error echo instead, which is a different bug and not the captured one), and the path traversal at files/?path=/etc/passwd at 02:24:02 returning root:x:0:0:. Your decoy work is excellent and earns full marks: you named the tempting hand-rolled HS256 verify branch, explained that hash_equals is constant-time so the timing-attack worry is unfounded, and correctly pointed at alg:none and the hardcoded secret as the true bugs. D2 reconstructs the chain in order with timestamps from recon at 02:14:08 through the 312-row exfil, and your full-chain vector correctly uses S:C to capture the scope change into the shared internal service. The SQLi vector AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N is right, but on the SQLi summary row you wrote Critical with no base number, so that hop is a bare label not a justified score, and Hop 5 conflates the forged-token step with the XXE and the path traversal so the PoC there does not cleanly match one capture line. Your impact is well reasoned: you extrapolated from the 20-row sample to NGN 62.5M across 312 customers with the averaging assumption stated openly, and you tied it to the BoltCash launch in 6 weeks, which is exactly the right move. D3 is the best deliverable. The exec summary is jargon-free and lands on the 312 customers and their balances, the threat model correctly identifies the 2021 modification that shares auth with /api/v1/internal, the findings carry evidence lines, the decoy is disproved correctly, and crucially your remediation table is ordered by risk reduction per hour of effort rather than raw CVSS, which is what Bayo actually needs. Your two stopgaps name the exact field (the legacy_admin_jwt cookie, the username arg) and give false-positive rates. D4 answers all four prompts in your own voice, anchors to 05-exfil-sample.csv and the alg:none finding, and makes ISC2 Canon II load-bearing. The one gap is the NDPA citation: you named the notify-NDPC and notify-data-subjects duties but did not cite the sections, which are section 40 (notify the NDPC within 72 hours) and section 41 (notify data subjects on high risk). The single most important fix is to catalogue all ten findings with their captured evidence lines, specifically the stored XSS cookie beacon at 02:18:47 and the path traversal at 02:24:02, because a complete findings table is what separates a strong report from a near-complete one.
